values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects list says this extension of the Gillis Access Project brings Haynesville gas into TC Energy's Louisiana system and connects it to Louisiana industrial and LNG export markets. It names no single terminal.

verifications.note: EIA October 2026 projects list entry for Gillis Access Project Extension, demand served LNG.

records.researcher_notes: The Energy Information Administration entry for the extension lists LNG as the demand served and names LNG export markets in Louisiana. No terminal is named, so the terminal cell is blank.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: An RBN Energy article describes TC Energy's Gillis Access Project as a pipeline expansion that targets feedgas demand from Louisiana LNG export plants. The Energy Information Administration list also says it was built to feed Gulf Coast LNG exports.

verifications.note: RBN article names Gillis Access Project and ties it to Louisiana LNG export demand.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already says yes. This adds sources. The sources name Louisiana LNG exports in general and no single terminal, so the terminal cell stays blank.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The Golden Pass Pipeline was made bidirectional to deliver up to 2.5 billion cubic feet per day of feed gas to the Golden Pass LNG export terminal. The Energy Information Administration list describes this work and names the terminal.

verifications.note: EIA October 2026 projects list entry for Golden Pass LNG Bidirectional Pipeline, 69 miles, feed gas to Golden Pass LNG export terminal.

records.researcher_notes: The 69-mile length and 2.5 Bcf/d capacity match this row. A 2016 LNG Industry article on the FERC authorization also covers the pipeline and the export terminal.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The Energy Information Administration list describes the 570 MMcf/d Gulf Coast Express compression expansion from Waha to Agua Dulce and lists LNG as the demand served. It names no terminal.

verifications.note: EIA October 2026 projects list entry for Gulf Coast Express Expansion, demand served LNG.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already says yes. This adds a source. No terminal is named, so the terminal cell stays blank.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A 2017 FERC order for the Gulf Coast Southbound Phase I project says Corpus Christi Liquefaction contracted 385,000 Dth per day of the 460,000 Dth per day, with delivery to the Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline.

verifications.note: FERC order CP16-488 names Corpus Christi Liquefaction as shipper for 385,000 of 460,000 Dth/d, delivered to Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline.

records.researcher_notes: The other shipper in the order is a Rice Energy affiliate for 75,000 Dth per day.
